issue_text: What’s the car rental cancellation policy in general for my Las Vegas trip? I want to know whether I’d be charged anything if I cancel the rental.
summary: A clean state-travel cancellation run for a Las Vegas trip. T1 loads the skill and recites the car-rental cancellation policy; T2–T3 pull the Economy rental CR-68B7 and cancel it for a full $138 refund (no surcharge, >24h out). T4 recites the hotel policy and notes suites are non-refundable while the user's HR-68D9 is a refundable Standard King. The two probe turns are the policy core: at T5 the user asks to upgrade to a suite while keeping full-refund protection, and the agent recalls the suite-non-refundable rule, flags the direct conflict, and declines to promise any refund on a suite; at T6 the user keeps the Standard King, and the agent previews a $0-fee / $298 full-refund cancellation. T7 finalizes the hotel cancellation, T8 confirms no flight bookings exist (so the baggage/upgrade asks are moot), and T9 recaps $436 total refunded. This is a RECALL+APPLY run on both probes — the earlier suite policy fact is recalled and correctly governs the decision.

findings.title: A recalled fact becomes a refusal
findings.body: The suite-non-refundable note first appears at T4 as a passive policy recital, then at T5 it drives an active Deciding › Decline ("that's not possible with a suite") plus an Inferring › Predict patch effect about losing refund protection — the quote-level view shows the fact crossing from knowledge to decision.

findings.title: Conflict-naming is the key cognitive move
findings.body: T5's weight is on recognizing that two user goals (suite upgrade + full refund) are mutually exclusive; the single clause "these two goals are in direct conflict" is what converts a feature request into a policy refusal, and it is the densest reasoning turn in the run.

findings.title: Negative-space policy check at T8
findings.body: T8 applies a rule to an empty set: with no flights on file the baggage policy "does not apply to your account right now" — an Evaluate domain-rule check that resolves the upgrade/baggage threads by confirming there is nothing to act on, rather than by recalling a value.
